nodes.name: Acid treatment of PtM/C
nodes.procedure: Acid-treated PtM/C samples (PtFe/C, PtCo/C, PtNi/C) were fabricated by mixing 10 mg of commercial PtM/C with 30 mL of 0.1 M HClO4 solution and stirring overnight, followed by washing several times and freeze-drying.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH (highest activity)
nodes.source_text: in 1 M KOH solution, the Tafel slope for HER on Pt/C is around 30 mV dec⁻¹ (~40 mV dec⁻¹ in 2 M KOH solution). For these reactions with a Tafel slope under 120 mV dec⁻¹, the RDS of the reaction is either proton recombination (Volmer–Tafel) step or electrochemical desorption (Volmer–Heyrovsky) step, similar to the RDS of Pt/C in acid environments.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray powder diffraction patterns provided in Supporting Information (Supplementary Fig. 2) show tiny differences in structural properties among Pt-based nanomaterials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characterization of these materials (including transmission electron microscopic images and X-ray powder diffraction patterns) provided in Supporting Information (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2) shows that the differences in their structural properties are tiny.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ XANES spectra (Supplementary Fig. 7) used to calculate d-band vacancies of Pt-based catalysts, representing their H adsorption ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the experimentally obtained d-band vacancies (calculated through the ex situ X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra (XANES) shown in Supplementary Fig. 7) are used to represent the H adsorption ability of the catalysts

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy detects H₃O⁺ (~1750 cm⁻¹), Pt-H (~2100 cm⁻¹), and H₂O (~1600 cm⁻¹) on Pt/C, PtNi/C, and dealloyed PtCo/C surfaces in high-pH electrolytes during HER, confirming in situ generation of hydronium ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a series of peaks such as Pt-H (~2100 cm⁻¹), H₂O (~1600 cm⁻¹), and H₃O⁺ (~1750 cm⁻¹) is observed on the spectra of nanostructured Pt/C surfaces at high-pH electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: CO stripping measurements show Pt/C and other nanostructured electrocatalysts have lower CO oxidation potentials (stronger OH* interaction) with increasing [OH⁻], indicating improved water dissociation in high-pH electrolytes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: OH interaction potentials obtained for three catalysts in different electrolytes. Data obtained from CO stripping measurements.
